C1. Electrical performance can couple local rework to neighbouring heat

Assume four diffusive metal-like bridges, constant electrical resistance R each, and a Lorenz-law electronic heat flux:
Q = n*L/(2R)*(Tj_K^2-Tn_K^2).
The assumed L is2.44e-8Wohm/K2. It is not asserted for every real contact or nonmetal. Constant R and all other heat paths are assumptions.

Joint and neighbour heat capacities are4e-5J/K each; each loses heat to25C through2e-4W/K. A.2W local heater warms the joint to140C and supplies introduced latent heat2mJ. Release is provisionally defined at95% melted fraction. The enthalpy/temperature law includes the melting plateau. Heater stops at that event and the whole subsequent cooling trajectory is retained. This does not construct wetting, retention or a working release.

With R=.01ohm, room-temperature aggregate bridge conductance is.00290994W/K. At the introduced.1A operating current, each contact drops1mV. Release occurs at.06201s/12.402mJ, neighbour130.782C at release and134.469C peak during the full trajectory, above the introduced80C limit.

With R=.1ohm, conductance is tenfold smaller, but operating drop is10mV and dissipation1mW/contact at.1A. Release occurs at.04057s/8.114mJ; neighbour47.628C at release but75.503C later. This simpler resistance trade can pass the introduced temperature limit. It is not legitimate to claim an isolating mechanism is always necessary.

Alternatively, retaining R=.01ohm during useful operation while reducing the bridge's thermal conduction to1% during rework gives.03568s/7.136mJ and34.474C neighbour peak. This is a conditional opening only: opening/isolating those real contacts, holding the part, protecting neighbours, accessing the interface and restoring low resistance are unconstructed physical operations. Turning power off alone does not remove thermal conduction. Substrate, fluid, radiation and mechanical bridges must also be counted; suppressing only the electrical bridge does not establish a complete temperature map.

The numerical integration preserves input energy as stored enthalpy plus neighbour heat plus ambient loss, with residual below1e-9J. Halving the time step changes the first neighbour peak by about.000144C. These numerical checks do not validate the thermal law or an actual material.
